utility.notes: Anaheim Public Utilities is the City of Anaheim's own municipal electric utility. Anaheim is notably absent from SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (which lists neighboring Orange County cities like Orange, Garden Grove, Tustin, Costa Mesa, Huntington Beach, Newport Beach, Westminster, Brea, and Yorba Linda but not Anaheim), consistent with Anaheim having its own municipal utility rather than SCE service.

value.name: Anaheim Public Utilities (APU)
value.notes: APU is a vertically-integrated municipal utility (like LADWP, Pasadena Water and Power, and Alameda Municipal Power) — it generates/procures and delivers its own power rather than sitting alongside a separate CCA. No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Anaheim in the sources reviewed this session.

permit_authority.value: City of Anaheim Planning & Building Department

interconnection_url.notes: Anaheim Public Utilities' own page states Anaheim uses 'NEM 2.0,' described as 'a wholesale-based rate NEM program,' and that the city 'is not going to NEM 3.0' — a distinctive municipal-utility policy choice, since NEM 3.0 (NBT) is a CPUC mandate that applies only to the three large investor-owned utilities (PG&E, SCE, SDG&E), not to municipal utilities like APU.

value.name: Battery Storage Rebate
value.description: APU's own battery storage rebate. Requires a UL-certified energy storage system with a minimum 5kWh capacity, hardwired and installed as part of an existing solar PV system, storing electricity produced by the customer's own solar PV, wind, or other residential generation. Customer must agree to be on a Time of Use rate and APU's MyPower Savings Program for at least 12 months.
value.eligibility: APU residential customers installing a UL-certified, hardwired battery energy storage system (minimum 5kWh) as part of an existing solar PV system, who enroll in a Time of Use rate and MyPower Savings Program for at least 12 months.

value.name: Engineering plans (submitted to Anaheim Planning & Building online for review)

required_documents.notes: The page does not enumerate a detailed checklist beyond referencing engineering plan submittal.

value: Customer can operate the system after Anaheim Planning & Building signs off — Anaheim Public Utilities does not itself issue Permission to Operate

value.program_or_pathway: Streamlined Permitting Process for Small Residential Rooftop Solar Energy Systems
other_conditions: Systems under 10kW are issued a permit without review
Existing NEM 1.0 customers remain grandfathered on NEM 1.0 unless they expand their system, at which point they convert fully to NEM 2.0

permit_fees.notes: No fee amount is listed on the city's page.
